prompt: Implement the Iterator pattern by hand: CircularHistory stores the newest entries in a wrap-around array, and its own Iterator must walk them from oldest to newest.
explanation: Implementing Iterable<String> is what lets a for-each loop work on your own class; the iterator you return holds the traversal state so the aggregate itself stays unchanged. The ring stores entry number n at index n % capacity, so the oldest surviving entry is at index (added - size) % capacity and each step moves forward modulo the capacity. next() must check hasNext() first and throw NoSuchElementException, which is the contract every Iterator promises.
hints: add can write to items[added % items.length] and then increase added -- the modulo does the wrapping for you.
size() is Math.min(added, items.length): before the buffer fills, it is just the number of adds.
In iterator(), capture how many entries to yield and the starting index before returning the anonymous Iterator, then keep a counter of how many you have already handed out.
